attempts.prompt:
Flat orthographic game texture concept: one face of a heavy hewn oak beam from the timber frame of a house in a damp late-medieval harbour town, seen straight on; camera perpendicular, no perspective, no rounded shading, flat even shadowless light. The face is an upright band exactly half as wide as tall, 768 by 1536 pixels, centred on the canvas with plain light grey margins left and right; it fills the band edge to edge.

[FORM — keep exactly] One solid squared timber, dressed flat with an adze: fine straight lengthwise grain and faint shallow adze marks, no bark, no wavy grain. Three dark shrinkage cracks along the grain, of different lengths: one runs nearly the whole length, two are shorter and stop partway; they are narrow and slightly irregular. One thin flat hand-forged iron strap across the beam about a quarter of the way down from the top, its height about a tenth of the band width, plain dull iron with rust, two small flat nail heads near its two ends.

[COLOUR AND AGEING] The darkest wood in town: very dark olive brown, mean colour close to sRGB 41, 35, 21, low saturation. Damp from the sea: large flat dark olive damp stains, a few soft dark green patches in and beside the cracks, a dull rust stain below the strap. Old and wet but sound.

[STYLE] Painterly but readable material reference; the look of a dark late-medieval game from the early 2000s, remade with better craft; muted, low saturation, low contrast; clean surface without generator noise, white specks or scale-like stroke patterns.

[AVOID — rejected before] Bark, wavy flowing grain, scaly strokes. Bright yellow-green moss clumps. A beam that reads as planks. A thick band, domed rivets, a tread pattern on the iron. Light or saturated wood. Painted light and shadow. Text, people, props.

Texture edit of the WOODBEAM_02 oak beam image from your most recent step in this thread (the one with the wandering crack). Keep exactly: the band and its margins, the straight grain, the iron strap with its two nails and its place, the blotchy dark olive damp stains, the colour and the style.

[CHANGE ONLY] The cracks: three long, deep, narrow cracks running straight along the grain, vertically, each most of the length of the beam, slightly wavy and irregularly spaced: two close together a little right of the centre, one near the left edge. Remove the crack that runs diagonally across the grain. Keep two short narrow cracks elsewhere.

[AVOID — rejected before] Cracks across the grain. Cracks at equal distances that split the face into planks. Bark. Painted light and shadow.

Edit of the WOODBEAM_02 oak beam image you generated first in this thread. Keep the band and its margins, the straight grain, the iron strap with its two nails and its place, the colour and the style.

[CHANGE ONLY] More shrinkage cracks: two long dark cracks running the whole length of the beam and three or four shorter ones, all narrow and slightly irregular, following the grain. More damp: large flat dark olive damp stains over about a third of the face, darker around the cracks and below the strap.

[AVOID — rejected before] Wide lens-shaped cracks. Bark or wavy grain. Bright moss clumps. Lighter wood. Painted light and shadow.

Not an image_gen prompt: the frame beam NW_CITY_WOODBEAM_02 built as a 3D model in Blender and baked.
Tool: scripts/content/timber_bake.py (layout beam02 --seed 0; render 1024 px, 128 samples, no sun, --wood city-timber-oak/reference-attempt-1.png; compose --seed 0) with scripts/content/piece_bake.py and scripts/content/mesh3d/blender/piece_scene.py.
Model: one face of a hewn oak beam in the texture's own proportions (0.5 x 1.0 m; the game stretches it about 3.4 times along the beam), a 1 x 1 mm grid of heights: overlapping adze scallops, fine grain, weathered pockets along the grain, worn arrises. The original's cracks at its measured places: the main one along the whole length past the seam with a step near its lower end, up to 3.6 cm wide and 5.5 cm deep; a second one through the upper half; two short ones top left and right. An iron strap at v 0.22-0.27 over the face's high points, hammered and pitted, with two dome nails at u 0.16 and 0.81.
Weathering by the model's passes: the oak's grain calmed and turned the original's dark olive brown, light streaks grey-olive; damp blotches and pale weathered patches with sharp edges; the wood above the strap darker; damp along the cracks; rust and dirt washed down from the strap in columns; the crack insides black from the crevice AO; a tone curve (1.3). Roughness: dry wood 0.86-0.95, damp 0.74, strap 0.72, nails 0.6.

Edit of the WOODBEAM_02 oak beam image you generated first in this thread (the original one, not its later edit). Keep the band and its margins, the straight grain, the iron strap with its two nails and its place, the colour and the style.

[CHANGE ONLY] The cracks wander and are not parallel: one long crack starts at the top edge a little left of centre and drifts to the right, ending about four fifths of the way down; a second long crack rises from the bottom edge near the right side and fades out two thirds of the way up; three or four short narrow cracks elsewhere at different angles along the grain. No crack divides the face into equal strips. Damp: large uneven dark olive stains over about a third of the face, blotchy, with darker cores, around the cracks and below the strap.

[AVOID — rejected before] Straight parallel cracks at equal distances. A beam that reads as planks. Smooth even wear. Bark or wavy grain. Bright moss clumps. Painted light and shadow.
